patient_information: A 3-year-old rural Lao boy, developing normally, up to date with vaccinations; his parents are rice farmers.
chief_complaint: Gradual, painful swelling of the right cheek with associated fever and poor appetite for 10 days, and purulent discharge from the ear for 3 days.
history_of_present_illness: A 3-year-old rural Lao boy presented with a 10-day history of gradual, painful swelling of the right cheek with associated fever and poor appetite; 3 days prior, his mother noticed a purulent discharge from the ear; he had no cough, vomiting or diarrhoea; no history of previous ear infection, dental problems, or trauma; he was developing normally and was up to date with vaccinations.
exposure_and_epidemiology: From rural Laos, with parents who are rice farmers, indicating likely exposure to soil and water containing B. pseudomallei in paddy fields.
physical_exam: The child looked unwell; there was a localized, fluctuant, hot, tender swelling (6-8 cm in diameter) below and anterior to the right ear, extending from the lower cheek to the submandibular region, consistent with a parotid mass; ear examination revealed purulent discharge in the auditory canal and suspicion of a small fistula; a right lower motor neuron facial nerve palsy was present; oral cavity and throat were unremarkable; no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly; heart sounds were normal and chest was clear.
labs_and_diagnostics: WBC 16.5 x10^9/L (normal 4–10 x10^9/L), 90% neutrophils; Hb 9.4g/dL (normal 13-15g/dL); all other initial blood tests were normal. Pus culture from the right ear and parotid abscess isolated B. pseudomallei; blood culture was negative; chest radiography and abdominal ultrasound were normal.
differential_diagnosis: Acute bacterial parotitis (Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, Haemophilus influenzae, Gram-negative bacteria, Streptococcus pneumoniae), Burkholderia pseudomallei (melioidosis), Actinomycosis, cat-scratch disease (Bartonella henselae), mumps, parainfluenza viruses, influenza A, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, enteroviruses, granulomatous parotitis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare, other mycobacteria), salivary stones, and malignancies.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient underwent incision and drainage of the parotid with removal of copious pus, followed by 10 days of intravenous ceftazidime and 16 weeks of oral co-amoxiclav, resulting in a good clinical response with no complications or identified underlying disease.
final_diagnosis: Suppurative parotitis due to Burkholderia pseudomallei (Melioidosis).

images.caption: A Lao boy with a unilateral parotid mass showing signs of local inflammation.
